_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::ale#3, and the execution that FALSIFIED its original wording. The entry said realistic (steel) E values make the ALE mesh 'too stiff and prevent geometry tracking'. On the upstream ale2d_solid deck, YOUNG 250 -> 2.1e11 leaves the node-3 displacement unchanged to better than 1e-12: the deck's own result test still passes, because stand-alone ALE mesh motion is a Dirichlet-driven problem with no load, where a uniform stiffness scaling cancels. NUE 0.3 -> 0.49 does move it (1.2e-1 in x). The knowledge entry was rewritten to say that, and this fixture holds the corrected version. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the discriminating arm: make the 'steel' deck identical to the soft one. STEEL then no longer demonstrates anything, but more to the point the NUE contrast is what carries the corrected claim — so mutate NUE back to the baseline and the fixture must go red.

invert the pathology the other way: give the steel arm a stiffness change that DOES bite (a per-element material contrast is emulated by changing NUE too), so UNIFORM_YOUNG_SCALING would no longer be the thing observed.
